newsitem.title: SPAIN: Dollar drop, Wall St hit Madrid stocks at close.
newsitem.headline: Dollar drop, Wall St hit Madrid stocks at close.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed sharply lower on Wednesday as the bourse was unnerved by a late drop in the dollar and Wall Street volatility.
Stocks blipped upward after Wall Street opened higher, recovering some earlier losses, but then reversed sharply as the Dow Jones showed weakness.
The general index fell 7.56 points, 1.26 percent, to 590.43 and the Ibex-35 lost 94.4 points, 1.39 percent, to 6,723.42.

"We recovered part of what was lost on Wall Street, but then it was seen that the Dow Jones couldn't recover and later it turned sharply, coinciding with a sharp drop in the dollar and this caused intense nervousness in European markets," a dealer said.
Derivatives-linked trading was also moving the Madrid bourse. U.S. CPI and industrial production figures due on Thursday were expected to be the focus of attention.
There were some rumours about a delay in the euro launch that triggered some selling, but they were dismissed by dealers as typical of summer holiday reactions.
